purpose: Text-mode MIME database snapshot the round-96 C1 candidate and the round-95 oracle are answered against: the 8 text files of the host DB with no mime.cache in any reachable dir (glib text mode, xdgmime.c:129-206).

source.access: read-only: files copied with cp(1); the source tree was never written

copy_recipe: for f in magic globs globs2 aliases subclasses icons generic-icons XMLnamespaces; do cp "/usr/share/mime/$f" "$S/hostdb/mime/$f"; done
cd "$S/hostdb/mime" && sha256sum magic globs globs2 aliases subclasses icons generic-icons XMLnamespaces  # must equal the pins below
for f in ...; do cmp -s "/usr/share/mime/$f" "$f"; done  # byte identity, measured 8/8 identical
find "$S/hostdb" -name mime.cache  # must print nothing; measured 0 hits

assertions.env_for_text_mode: HOME=$S/empty-h XDG_DATA_HOME=$S/empty-dh XDG_DATA_DIRS=$S/hostdb -> no reachable mime.cache, so glib answers in text mode

excluded_from_copy: mime.cache (cache-mode marker; its presence in any reachable dir means cache mode, outside the r96 C1 surface)
per-type subdirs (application/, audio/, ... ), packages/, treemagic, types, version
cross_check: globs2 sha256 556ee69c8be2e24c4e3025dc5af0bdae71c6dca899491b4c95778a531958168e equals the round-94 counter's host /usr/share/mime/globs2 pin (harm-final-r95.txt), so the DB has not drifted since round 94.
